mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates a strong economy, leading to higher corporate earnings and thus positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in unemployment signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate revenues, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If unemployment drops below 3.5% but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth and unemployment both indicate economic strength, their combined effect enhances S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If both GDP growth and unemployment are favorable but S&P 500 returns are not.

mechanism_narrative: Higher federal funds rates increase borrowing costs, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If rates rise above 2.5% but S&P 500 returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production signals strong economic output, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production rises but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: Job market expansion, indicated by increasing PAYEMS, boosts economic activity and S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts indicate strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If housing starts rise but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) rises and federal funds rates are high, the combined effect negatively impacts S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
regime_hint: high inflation and tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If both inflation rises and rates are high but S&P 500 returns are positive.
